cards.text: Paul is writing to Timothy, the one he calls his beloved child (2 Timothy 1:2). He's just warned him that in the last days, men will oppose the truth (2 Timothy 3:1-8). Now Paul turns the spotlight on Timothy himself: "You, however,…"

cards.question: Paul says Timothy has watched him up close. What has Timothy observed?

answers.text: Paul's teaching and the way he lives
Paul's travels and the letters he sends
Paul's friends and the money he earns

cards.text: The list keeps rolling: his purpose, his faith, his patience, his love, his perseverance. Then it takes a hard turn.

cards.question: Where does Paul's list of what Timothy has observed turn next?

cards.text: Paul even names the towns: Antioch, Iconium and Lystra. In Lystra, they stoned him and dragged him out of the city, figuring he was dead (Acts 14:19).
"What persecutions I endured!" Paul says. Friend, I spent YEARS complaining about dust in a junk drawer, and this man got hit with rocks and got right back up (Acts 14:20).

cards.question: After all those persecutions in Antioch, Iconium and Lystra, how does Paul say it ended?

answers.text: The Lord rescued him from all of them
The towns finally welcomed him in
He learned to stay out of trouble

cards.text: Then Paul zooms out. This part isn't only about Paul anymore.

cards.question: Paul says all who desire to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be ___.
While godly believers face persecution, what does Paul say happens to evil men and imposters?

answers.text: They go from bad to worse

cards.question: Paul says the imposters fool other people but never get fooled themselves.

cards.text: "deceiving and being deceived." The scammer is getting SCAMMED, friend, and his phone is full of texts about his car's extended warranty.
The imposters are going from bad to worse. Then Paul turns right back to Timothy: "But as for you,…"

cards.question: With imposters going from bad to worse, what does Paul tell Timothy to do?

answers.text: Continue in what he has learned
Look for a fresh new teaching

cards.question: Why can Timothy trust the things he has learned and firmly believed?

answers.text: He knows who he learned them from
He worked them out on his own

cards.text: And Timothy didn't pick this stuff up last week. Paul reminds him how far back it goes.

cards.question: Timothy first came to know the Holy Scriptures after he met Paul.

cards.text: From infancy! Timothy had the Scriptures before he had TEETH. Me? I didn't know what a cookie was until somebody pressed me into my first batch of dough.

cards.question: Paul says the Holy Scriptures are able to make Timothy wise for ___ through faith in Christ Jesus.

cards.text: Then Paul tells Timothy where ALL Scripture comes from.

cards.question: Where does Paul say all Scripture comes from?

cards.text: And Scripture isn't just for sitting on a shelf. Paul says it's useful, and he lists the ways.

cards.question: Paul says Scripture is useful for instruction but not for correcting anyone.

cards.text: Instruction, conviction, correction and training in righteousness. Friend, I've been corrected by a recipe card more times than I'd like to admit, so I KNOW correction works.

cards.question: Paul says Scripture does all that so the man of God may be complete and what else?

answers.text: Fully equipped for every good work

findings.problem: Paul shows up for the first time with no word on who he is. Timothy is introduced only through what Paul calls him, so the baker isn't told who Paul is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The setup line "Then it takes a hard turn" rules out the wrong answer "To his rewards and honors" on card 4. That leaves only the right answer and "regrets and mistakes", so the setup does the choosing for the baker.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "I spent YEARS complaining about dust in a junk drawer" adds a new habit to his drawer years, and it goes against the backstory. There, he gave up on himself, "didn't talk much", and later spent his time welcoming newcomers. Made-up moments are allowed only around his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The joke blends the modern comparison with the Bible setting. The imposters Paul describes are the ones getting scammed, and they have phones full of texts about a car's extended warranty. The comparison should be one everyday image of its own.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: This card repeats 2 Timothy 3:13, which cards 10 and 11 already covered and answered. It doesn't move the passage forward. It's a recap with a joke attached.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't land. Timothy knew the Scriptures from infancy, so from the very start. Papa Dorin learned what a cookie was at his first batch, which is also from the very start, so there's no contrast and the punchline reads as "huh?". The line "somebody pressed me into my first batch of dough" also gets him backwards: he's the stamper that presses the dough. It also adds a new detail to his backstory.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
